Sr. Developer Advocate, AI and Machine Learning
Sr. Developer Advocate, AI and Machine Learning

reading.body:
Developer Relations and Education roles in AI are scarce in tracked job markets, with only three open positions as of September 2026, all focused on building practitioner communities rather than core research or deployment.

The three openings span instructor and advocate roles at established companies. CHESS posted a full-time instructor position in Albuquerque at $65,209 annually. Databricks posted two identical senior developer advocate roles in San Francisco and Seattle. All three entries categorize as developer relations and education rather than engineering, research, or operations. The salary data is limited to a single federal or institutional rate and does not capture market range for private sector roles.

This category remains marginal in hiring volume compared to other AI functions. The data does not distinguish between roles that build AI capacity directly versus those that distribute knowledge of existing tools. It also does not capture whether developer advocate hiring has grown, shrunk, or plateaued, since only a single snapshot is provided. Geographic concentration in California and one outlier in New Mexico suggests hiring follows where companies operate their development centers rather than independent distribution.
